extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, package designers, and regulatory compliance personnel handling Class 7 (radioactive) material transport
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for determining A1/A2 radionuclide values, exempt activity concentrations and consignment limits, mixture and grouping rules, and labeling/shipping-paper obligations for transporting Class 7 radioactive materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity limits for Type B(U) and Type B(M) packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The limits on activity contained in a Type B(U) or Type B(M) package are those prescribed in §§ 173.416 and 173.417, or in the applicable approval certificate under §§ 173.471, 173.472 or 173.473.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the activity limits specified in the cited sections or the approval certificate for a particular package design; do not rely on other values for Type B packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tables for radionuclides listed in §§ 173.435 and 173.436
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual radionuclides listed in the table in § 173.435 and § 173.436: (1) A1 and A2 values are given in the table in § 173.435; and (2) Activity concentration exemption values and consignment activity exemption values are given in the table in § 173.436.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a radionuclide appears in these tables, the tabulated A1/A2 and exemption values are the basic radionuclide values to be used in transport calculations, labeling, and exemption determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted values for radionuclides not listed in tables
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual radionuclides which are not listed in the tables in § 173.435 or § 173.436: (1) the radionuclide values in Tables 7 or 8 of this section may be used; or (2) other basic radionuclide values may be used provided they are first approved by the Associate Administrator or, for international transport, multilateral approval is obtained from the pertinent Competent Authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not listed, use the general default values (Tables 7/8) or obtain formal approval for other values; retain approvals for inspection and international movement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of solubility-class A2 when chemical form known
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the chemical form of each radionuclide is known, it is permissible to use the A2 value related to its solubility class as recommended by the International Commission on Radiological Protection, if the chemical forms under both normal and accident conditions of transport are taken into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using solubility-class-based A2 values, ensure assessment accounts for both normal and accident conditions and the chemical forms expected under each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of single radioactive decay chains
rubrics_metrics.description: A single radioactive decay chain in which the radionuclides are present in their naturally-occurring proportions, and in which no daughter nuclide has a half life either longer than 10 days or longer than that of the parent nuclide, will be considered as a single radionuclide, and the activity to be taken into account and the A1 or A2 value to be applied will be those corresponding to the parent nuclide of that chain. Otherwise, the parent and daughter nuclides will be considered as a mixture of different nuclides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check daughter nuclide half-lives relative to 10 days and to the parent's half-life to decide whether to treat the chain as a single radionuclide (use parent's A1/A2) or as a mixture (apply mixture formulas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixture rule for special form Class 7 material (Type A packages)
rubrics_metrics.description: For special form Class 7 (radioactive) material, the activity which may be transported in a Type A package must satisfy: [formula using B(i) and A1(i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the provided summation formula (symbols defined: B(i) = activity of radionuclide i in special form; A1(i) = A1 value for radionuclide i) to ensure combined activities do not exceed Type A limits. (The regulatory text supplies the explicit formula.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixture rule for normal form Class 7 material (Type A packages)
rubrics_metrics.description: For normal form Class 7 (radioactive) material, the activity which may be transported in a Type A package must satisfy: [formula using C(j) and A2(j)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the provided summation formula (C(j) = activity of radionuclide j in normal form; A2(j) = A2 value for radionuclide j) to demonstrate compliance with Type A activity limits for mixtures of normal form radionuclides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined special and normal form mixture rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the package contains both special and normal form Class 7 (radioactive) material, the activity which may be transported in a Type A package must satisfy: [combined formula].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the combined formula provided in the regulation to account for both special form (A1-based) and normal form (A2-based) contributions when both are present in a single package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative determination of A1 for mixtures of special form material
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatively, the A1 value for a mixture of special form material may be determined as follows: [formula using f(i) and A1(i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute mixture A1 as a weighted function of component fractions f(i) (fraction of activity for radionuclide i) and the component A1 values; use this alternative when appropriate and as specified in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative determination of A2 for mixtures of normal form material
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatively, the A2 value for mixtures of normal form material may be determined as follows: [formula using f(i) and A2(i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute mixture A2 using activity fractions and component A2 values per the regulatory formula when the alternative method is chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt activity concentration calculation for mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: The exempt activity concentration for mixtures of nuclides may be determined as follows: [formula using f(i) and [A](i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified mixture formula where [A](i) is the activity concentration for exempt material containing nuclide i and f(i) is the fraction of activity concentration; apply when evaluating exemption eligibility for mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt consignment activity limit calculation for mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: The activity limit for an exempt consignment for mixtures of nuclides may be determined as follows: [formula using f(i) and A(i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided formula with f(i) (fraction of activity of nuclide i) and A(i) (activity limit for exempt consignments for nuclide i) to determine if a consignment qualifies for exemption as a mixture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping when identities known but individual activities unknown (A1/A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the identity of each nuclide is known but the individual activities of some of the radionuclides are not known, the radionuclides may be grouped and the lowest A1 or A2 value, as appropriate, for the radionuclides in each group may be used in applying the formulas in paragraphs (d)(1) through (d)(5) of this section. Groups may be based on the total alpha activity and the total beta/gamma activity when these are known, using the lowest A1 or A2 values for the alpha emitters or beta/gamma emitters, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individual component activities are unknown, create groups (e.g., alpha vs beta/gamma), apply the lowest A1/A2 in that group in mixture formulas; document grouping rationale and used values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping when identities known but individual activities unknown (exempt concentrations and consignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the identity of each nuclide is known but the individual activities of some of the radionuclides are not known, the radionuclides may be grouped and the lowest [A] (activity concentration for exempt material) or A (activity limit for exempt consignment) value, as appropriate, for the radionuclides in each group may be used in applying the formulas in paragraphs (d)(6) and (d)(7) of this section. Groups may be based on the total alpha activity and the total beta/gamma activity when these are known, using the lowest [A] or A values for the alpha emitters or beta/gamma emitters, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grouping and lowest exemption values for groups when component activities are unknown to determine exemption eligibility for mixtures; record grouping basis and chosen values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of radionuclides to show on shipping papers and labels for mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: For mixtures of radionuclides, the radionuclides (n) that must be shown on shipping papers and labels in accordance with §§ 172.203 and 172.403 of this subchapter, respectively, must be determined on the basis of the following formula: [formula where n + m represents all radionuclides; m are the radionuclides that do not need to be considered; a(i) is the activity of radionuclide i; and A(i) is the A1 or A2 value, as appropriate].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the regulation's selection formula to decide which radionuclides in a mixture must be named on shipping papers and package labels; use component activities and A1/A2 values per the formula and retain the selection calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Tables 7 and 8 (general/default values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables 7 and 8 provide general values for A1 and A2 (Table 7) and general exemption values (Table 8) for cases where only beta/gamma emitters are known, only alpha emitters are known, or no relevant data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specific radionuclide values are not available, use the Table 7 general A1/A2 defaults or Table 8 general exemption values according to which emission type(s) are known; these serve as fallback/default numeric values in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of § 173.435 A1/A2 numeric table and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The table of A1 and A2 values for radionuclides is provided in § 173.435 (numeric A1/A2 and specific activity values for many radionuclides). Notes include: (a) A1 and/or A2 values include contributions from daughter nuclides with half-lives less than 10 days; (b) reserved; (c) quantity may be determined from decay rate or radiation level measurement at prescribed distance; (d)/(e)/(f) specify uranium compound applicability by chemical form; (g) values apply to unirradiated uranium only; (h) special domestic values for Cf-252; (i) special domestic A2 for Mo-99.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a radionuclide appears, use the numeric A1/A2 and specific-activity values and apply the relevant notes (a–i) to interpret applicability, measurement method, or special domestic limits. Notes impose constraints (e.g., chemical-form-specific values for uranium compounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of § 173.436 exempt activity concentration and consignment limit table
rubrics_metrics.description: The Table of Exempt material activity concentrations and exempt consignment activity limits for radionuclides is provided in § 173.436 (numeric activity concentration (Bq/g, Ci/g) and activity limit for exempt consignment (Bq, Ci) by radionuclide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numeric exemption concentrations and consignment limits in § 173.436 to determine whether material or consignments qualify for exemption; apply the mixture and grouping rules in the regulation when mixtures are involved.
